h: The Consolation of Being Remembered at the Root

p: that the seven haftaros of consolation
correspond to the seven lower middos;
corresponds to the second middah, Gevurah,
which is the attribute of judgment.
"And My anger will flare against it on that day,
and I will hide My face from them," etc.;
And so it is written afterward:
הֲלֹא עַל כִּי אֵין אֱלֹהַי בְּקִרְבִּי
"Is it not because my God is not in my midst
that these evils have found me?"
Hashem has forsaken us, chas v'shalom.
"Why, O God, have You abandoned us forever?" etc.;
that is, with the Name Elokim,
which is the aspect of Gevurah,
And so it is explicit in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 97b):
we are waiting but He is not waiting;
'Therefore Hashem waits to be gracious to you,' etc.
The attribute of judgment is holding it back."
And so it is explicit in the pasuk:
"Therefore Hashem waits to be gracious to you,
and therefore He is exalted to have mercy on you,
for Hashem is a God of judgment."
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר בְּנֶחָמָה זוֹ (יְשַׁעְיָה מט, יד)
And that is why it says in this consolation (Yeshayahu 49:14):
"And Tziyon said: Hashem has forsaken me":
the Name of the attribute of mercy
"the law of the kingdom is the law"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קיח, א)
is also called the aspect of the Shechinah,
the Shechinah was with them, etc.,
and it did not forsake us.
that He forgot us, chas v'shalom, in the exile.
וְעַל זֶה מֵשִׁיב הַנָּבִיא (שָׁם מט, טו)
And to this the prophet answers (ibid. 49:15):
"Can a woman forget her nursing child,
lack compassion for the child of her womb?"
for the Shechinah is called by the name Mother,
as we find in the Gemara (Kiddushin 31b):
the sound of his mother's footsteps,
I will rise before the Shechinah that is coming."
וְאֵין אָבִיו אֶלָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵּי
"And 'his father' is none other than HaKadosh Baruch Hu," etc.,
וְאֵין אִמּוֹ אֶלָּא כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּלֵּי
"and 'his mother' is none other than Knesses Yisrael," etc.
For just as the middos of Chochmah and Binah
are called in the holy Zohar
that is, the middah of Tiferes,
is called by the name Father,
and Malchus is the aspect of Mother;
"Can a woman forget her nursing child,
lack compassion for the child of her womb?":
forgetting cannot be imagined of the Shechinah,
that is, even if it could be imagined, chas v'shalom,
and this follows what is said
'These are the generations of the heavens and the earth'";
that even if one could imagine
that He might forget all of creation,
And this follows what is said
בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רנו, ב)
"Anochi is from the side of Kesser,
for the letter kaf alludes to Kesser,
and there remain the letters of Ayin,
which is the aspect of Atika
לֹא יְצוּיַּר עוֹד שְׁכִיחָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
forgetting, chas v'shalom, can no longer be imagined.
"Therefore Hashem waits to be gracious to you,
and therefore He is exalted to have mercy on you":
יָרוּם מוֹרֶה עַל בְּחִינַת עַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא
"exalted" indicates the aspect of Atika Kadisha,
and this is "I will not forget you."
שֶׁשֵּׁם זֶה מוֹרֶה עַל ט׳ הַמִּדּוֹת
for this Name indicates the nine middos,
and its tip alludes to Kesser Elyon
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג סה, ב)
this is the event at Sinai";
that is, Hashem Yisbarach then said
for so "I am Hashem your God" indicates,
believes in Hashem as a matter of course,
because he is bound at the root.
וְזֶה מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (הַאֲזִינוּ שָׁם)
And this is what is written in the holy Zohar (Ha'azinu, ibid.):
"Rather, they are attached to His Name;
for they are attached to His very Name."
And this is along the lines of what is written
And this is "I will not forget you":
since they are bound at the root,
and attached to HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בְּכַמָּה דּוּכְתֵּי
as the holy Zohar writes in several places.
"But since the attribute of judgment is holding it back,
'Fortunate are all who wait for Him.'"
That is, through the hoping and the waiting
one merits that there truly enter the heart
And the pesukim of consolation are said on Shabbos,
a revelation of the aspect of Atika,
as written in the holy Zohar,
and especially at the second meal,
which is the meal of Atika;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יוּכַל הַיִּשְׂרָאֵל לִזְכּוֹת
and through this the Jew can merit
that this repose enter the heart,
which is "I will not forget you,"
that is, through the aspect of Anochi,
which indicates that they are bound at the root,
which is the aspect of Atika,
וְכֵן נִדְרַשׁ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב פט, א)
And so the holy Zohar expounds (II 89a)
"On the day that He gives rest," etc. (Yeshayahu 14:3),
as referring to the day of Shabbos,
on which repose enters the heart;
in the midst of the hard labor,
that everything is from Hashem Yisbarach
